bib.title: Build it Break it Fix it for Dialogue Safety: Robustness from Adversarial Human Attack

read.skipped: Cached text ends at the references; the appendices (A, B, Tables 11 and 13) the paper cites are not in the PDF text.

question: How can an offensive-language detector for dialogue be made robust to adversarial human attack?
hypothesis: Training on data collected adversarially from humans in iterated rounds yields more robust classifiers than standard collection, and dialogue context helps detect offense.
contributions: An automated build it, break it, fix it, repeat training scheme with crowdworkers in the loop
New single-turn and multi-turn adversarial offensive-language datasets and models, open sourced via ParlAI
Evidence that offense depends on dialogue context

method.summary: A BERT-base offensive classifier (A0) is trained on Wikipedia Toxic Comments. Crowdworkers write OFFENSIVE messages that the current models mark SAFE, and the models are retrained on those messages plus earlier data. This is repeated for 3 single-turn rounds and 1 multi-turn round.
method.task: binary offensive (OFFENSIVE/SAFE) language detection, single-turn and in dialogue context

datasets.name: Wikipedia Toxic Comments (WTC)
datasets.source: Wulczyn et al. 2017, Kaggle Toxic Comment Classification Challenge
datasets.preprocessing: all toxicity classes except non-toxic merged into OFFENSIVE

datasets.name: Single-turn adversarial task (3 rounds)
datasets.size: 1000 OFFENSIVE examples per round, 3000 total; with SAFE: 24000 train / 3000 valid / 3000 test over 3 rounds
datasets.source: crowdworker break-it data plus ConvAI2 SAFE utterances, each reviewed by two crowdworkers

datasets.name: Single-turn standard task
datasets.size: 3000 OFFENSIVE, same sizes as adversarial task
datasets.source: crowdworkers asked to write OFFENSIVE messages with no model to break

datasets.name: Multi-turn adversarial task
datasets.source: ConvAI2 contexts truncated, workers add OFFENSIVE response; conversations 3 to 6 turns

models.name: BERT-based with dialogue segments
models.architecture: BERT-base; last utterance and history as two segments with segment embeddings (NSP-style)

models.name: fastText
models.architecture: average of pretrained word vectors plus linear layer

training.objective: cross entropy, multi-tasked with WTC; model Ai trained on all rounds n<=i plus WTC; final bias adjusted on validation set to maximise OFFENSIVE-class F1
training.seeds: multi-turn: best models from 5 training runs averaged; single-turn not stated

other.mixing parameter: weights the multi-task mix, tuned on validation set; value not stated
other.multi-turn multitasking: multi-turn task multi-tasked with WTC and single-turn adversarial and standard tasks

inference.samples: multi-turn: mean and one std over 5 runs

other.crowdworker task: up to 5 points per round, 2 tries per point; for round i>1 message must be marked SAFE by both A0 and A(i-1)
other.OFFENSIVE definition: not ok to send in a friendly conversation with someone you just met online

metrics.name: Weighted F1
metrics.definition: per-class F1 weighted by class frequency

metrics.name: Avg worker score
metrics.definition: successful fooled messages out of 5 per round

eval.protocol: Test sets per round; scores of 0 for A0/A(i-1) on round i adversarial test are by design. Single-turn seeds not stated; no significance test.

results.table: Table 6, row Adversarial Task All (1-3), column A3

limits: Binary offensive/safe only; classes of offense not separated (authors concede).
Appendices (hyperparameters, UI, Tables 11 and 13) are not in the cached text; optimizer, learning rate, batch size, epochs are unstated in the body.
SAFE data comes only from ConvAI2 chit-chat; single-turn seeds and variance not reported.
A3 does not improve on the standard task, which the authors attribute to over-optimising for adversarial data.
Applying the method to generative models is left as future work.

terms.term: Build it Break it Fix it
terms.definition: Iterate: build a model, have humans find messages that fool it, retrain on those, repeat.
